narrative:
**Week of 2026-08-24 — Hugging Face developer activity**

Model downloads fell sharply, dropping 59.2% week over week to 3.77M across the 26,015 models tracked (down from roughly 9.2M the prior week), while model likes moved the opposite direction, rising 49.2% to 15,031. Space likes fell 10.8% to 659 across 6,028 spaces. The divergence between downloads and likes is large enough that a collection or ingestion artifact should be ruled out before it is read as a demand signal; with no 4-week or 12-week baselines available in this cut, we cannot yet say whether the download level is anomalous or a return to trend.

The clearest compositional story was GLM/Zhipu's expansion: 293 models this week versus roughly 58 the prior week (+405%), the largest family-level move in the data. It was echoed on the Spaces side, where GLM/Zhipu reached 2.53% of the 513 chat-assistant spaces (13 spaces, up from about 1). "Other-open" models also grew 39.0% to 6,233, while Qwen slipped 5.4% to 7,945 and Llama fell 13.3% to 1,031; DeepSeek (81, -24.3%) and NVIDIA Nemotron (74, -28.2%) both contracted. Qwen nonetheless remained the leading identified family and held the top share in coding spaces at 39.5% of 114 spaces (+12.3%). Two caveats: 9,472 models — 36.4% of the total — remain family-unknown, so family shares should be treated as shares of labeled models only, and family splits inside small use cases (3d-gaming n=28, education n=26, other n=20, robotics n=11) rest on cell counts in the single digits and are too few to report reliably.

Among Spaces, growth concentrated in the "other" bucket (2,025 spaces, +11.1%) and in smaller categories — music generation (65, +18.2%), robotics (48, +17.1%), scientific tools (192, +9.1%) — while video generation fell 14.3% to 270 and search/research fell 7.7% to 311. Gradio led SDK growth at 2,184 spaces (+6.6%) against static's 3,168 (+2.6%); Streamlit dropped 31.5% to 74. On capabilities, agentic was the only major technology to gain, at 6.69% penetration (+3.3%), while RAG fell to 2.54% (-27.7%) and vision-language to 6.47% (-7.1%); long-context sat at 0.20% (12 spaces), too small a base for a meaningful change read. By vertical, enterprise productivity rose 17.3% to 6.69% penetration and consumer rose 10.3% to 10.37%, while healthcare (-14.9%) and e-commerce/retail (-13.3%) declined. Next week, watch whether the download drop reverses and whether GLM/Zhipu's model count holds near 293 or proves to be a one-week bulk upload.
